subject: microbiology
title: Drumstick Spores, Tetanospasmin Mechanism and Tetanus Forms

steps.tx: **Drumstick spores** (terminal, spherical, wider than the bacillus) identify tetani morphologically in wound specimens and cultures, though clostridia sporulate poorly in tissue and other species share terminal spores. Spore position vocabulary (central oval perfringens, subterminal, terminal) is Gram stain shorthand examiners require precisely.
steps.say: Terminal round spore swells the rod into a drumstick; position is vocabulary, not proof alone.

left.title: Spore positions
points: Free spores after sporulation in culture

steps.tx: **Drumstick spores** are terminal, spherical, and wider than the rod, and they identify Clostridium tetani morphologically in wound specimens and cultures. Clostridia sporulate poorly in tissue, and other species can share terminal spores, so shape is not proof by itself. Spore position is Gram stain vocabulary that must be stated exactly: central oval for perfringens, subterminal for some species, and terminal for tetani.
steps.say: A round terminal spore wider than the rod gives tetani its drumstick outline in wounds and cultures. Sporulation is poor in tissue, and other clostridia can look similar. Position still matters: central oval, subterminal, or terminal.

vis.alt: A micrograph shows slender bacilli with round terminal spores wider than the rods, like drumsticks.
vis.caption: Terminal round spores swell the ends of tetanus bacilli into drumstick shapes on the Gram film. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Tetanospasmin molecularly** is a 150 kilodalton dichain zinc protease: heavy chain binds gangliosides and synaptic vesicle protein at motor terminals and drives retrograde transport, light chain cleaves VAMP2 in inhibitory terminals. Minute quantities (lethal dose micrograms) explainHTIG urgency and toxoid potency.
steps.say: A protease that rides nerves backwards to cut brake vesicles: potency measured in micrograms.

left.title: Heavy chain jobs
points: Delivery of light chain to interneuron cytosol

steps.tx: **Incubation and period of onset** grade tetanus: incubation injury to first symptom (usually 3 to 21 days), period of onset first symptom to first spasm (under 48 hours ominous), shorter in cephalic and neonatal forms, prognostic together with autonomic features for ventilation planning.
steps.say: Short incubation plus fast onset buys a ventilator early.

left.title: Timing definitions
points: Incubation: wound to trismus or local rigidity
Period of onset: first symptom to first reflex spasm
Unknown wound in a third of cases

right.title: Severity grading
points: Ablett grades I to IV traditions
ICU admission threshold low once spasms generalise

steps.tx: **Spatula test** (touching posterior pharynx provokes masseter spasm and biting instead of gag) is bedside tetanus specificity folklore with study support, differential including strychnine poisoning (glycine receptor blocked, no trismus prominence, awareness until late), rabies, hypocalcaemic tetany (Chvostek, carpopedal, different meaning of tetany entirely) and dystonic reactions.
steps.say: Biting the spatula supports tetanus; strychnine mimics without the wound and lockjaw story.

left.title: Tetanus differentials
points: Strychnine: convulsions between relaxations, no trismus lead
Hypocalcaemia: tetany not tetanus, QT long

right.title: Bedside clues
points: Wound may be trivial or healed

steps.tx: **Autonomic dysfunction** in severe tetanus (labile hypertension, tachycardia storms, arrhythmias, ileus, urinary retention second week) is the modern mortality driver, managed with magnesium sulphate infusions, clonidine, morphine, esmolol moments, deep sedation and sometimes prolonged neuromuscular blockade with ventilation and tracheostomy.
steps.say: After spasms, storms: autonomic tetanus kills in week two without magnesium and patience.

right.title: Storm answers
points: Short acting agents for labile swings

steps.tx: **Neonatal tetanus** follows unclean cord cutting and stump applications (soil, dung traditions) plus unimmunised mothers: stops sucking day 3 to 14, rigidity and spasms, mortality high without intensive care; elimination validated country by country via maternal toxoid (two doses pregnancy), clean delivery kits and surveillance of every case as programme failure.
steps.say: Every neonatal tetanus case is a maternal immunisation system failure with a name.

right.title: Elimination system
points: Maternal Td two dose minimum pregnancy
Clean hands, blade, cord care messages
Supplementary immunisation in high risk districts

steps.tx: **Localised and cephalic tetanus** teach toxin geography: local rigidity may remain or generalise (immunoglobulin still indicated), cephalic after head and ear wounds produces cranial nerve palsies (facial weak mimicking Bell's) with trismus and dysphagia, high generalisation, otitis media chronic portals cultured.
steps.say: Facial palsy plus lockjaw after ear infection is cephalic tetanus, not Bell's alone.

left.title: Localised
points: HTIG and toxoid both given (different sites)

steps.tx: **Tetanus immunoglobulin and toxoid together** (different syringes and sites, toxoid series completed) in cases and wound prophylaxis confuse students yearly: HTIG gives today's antibodies, toxoid builds next month's, disease itself builds none reliably because toxin binds before immune instruction completes.
steps.say: Borrow antibodies for today, vaccinate for tomorrow; the disease itself teaches the immune system nothing safe.

left.title: HTIG role
points: Equine serum where human unavailable with testing

right.title: Toxoid role
points: Start or complete 3 dose series in cases
